# Spec §11 — decisions: Dev tools (road map 11)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed; its condensed record is
`designs/adr/roadmap-11-dev-tools.md` (the original is `archive/roadmap-11.md`).
V-4 and V-5 come from the build-velocity road map, now closed: `designs/adr/build-velocity.md` (the original is `archive/build-velocity.md`).

- **V-1 — Dev tools are compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, and the shipping build is
  the Distribution configuration, which does not set it.** Debug and Release set the flag;
  `make app` builds Release, so every proof and agent session has the tools, and the binary
  that is verified is the optimised one rather than a Debug build that only resembles it. A
  compile-time flag rather than a launch flag, because the user does not want the code shipped
  at all, not merely switched off. `make dist` checks that the tools' names are absent from the
  Distribution binary and present in the Release one, and fails otherwise. The agent server
  itself (§7.9) is a product feature and stays in every build; only the dev tools go. Risk
  accepted: the flag-off path is compiled by `make dist` alone, not by `make typecheck`.
  **Amended by NM-6** (rename R0): `REELCUT_DEV_TOOLS` is now `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`.
- **V-2 — A dev tool is not an op and not a user-visible edit, but it is an ordinary tool.** It
  has no UI path to mirror, so the agent-parity rule asks nothing of it; it goes through the same
  catalog, handler table, argument gate and startup parity check as every product tool, merged
  in from `AgentServer+DevTools.swift` so the frozen `AgentServer.swift` takes wiring only.
- **V-3 — Screens are captured with `cacheDisplay(in:to:)`, never ScreenCaptureKit or
  `screencapture`.** No Screen Recording grant — which an ad-hoc-signed rebuild may lose, and
  which the agent's terminal does not have — so a capture never waits on a person. What that
  path cannot draw (the player layer, Metal) is filled from `render_frame`'s picture and the
  result says so; the capture is a picture of the chrome, and pixel claims about the VIDEO stay
  with `render_frame`.
- **V-4 — The edit loop and mutant tiers drive a Debug app; the run a phase records, the gate's
  build and every `release_only` proof are Release.** Amends V-1's 'the binary that is verified
  is the optimised one': `debug_release_proof.py` shows the two answer alike (`tools/list`,
  `get_project` and the catalog snapshot, compared parsed), render byte-for-byte alike, and
  export alike but for the movie header's creation and modification times; Debug is used for its
  rebuild time. Risk accepted: an optimiser-only defect is seen only by the recorded run.
- **V-5 — The Debug build is its own app: "Frame Job Debug", `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`, its
  own defaults domain, and an Alternate handler for `.framejob`, so a double-click opens the real
  Frame Job.** Debug-config settings only (`PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`, `RC_APP_NAME`,
  `RC_PROJECT_HANDLER_RANK`, read through `:default=` so Release and Distribution keep identical
  settings and Info.plist bytes). `PRODUCT_NAME` stays `Reelcut` (bundle, executable, module).
  The Application Support folder, its default socket and its keys stay shared; TCC grants are
  per id, so a TCC-dependent proof is Release-only.
  **Amended by NM-3** (rename R0): "Reelcut Debug" is now "Frame Job Debug"
  (`Frame Job Debug.app`, executable `Frame Job Debug`); `com.kgalligan.Reelcut.debug` is now
  `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`; `.reelcut` is now `.framejob`; the real Reelcut is now the
  real Frame Job (`com.kgalligan.FrameJob`); `RC_APP_NAME` is now gone: Debug sets
  `PRODUCT_NAME` to "Frame Job Debug", `CFBundleName` and `CFBundleDisplayName` read
  `$(PRODUCT_NAME)`, and `RC_PROJECT_HANDLER_RANK` stays, read through `:default=`;
  "`PRODUCT_NAME` stays `Reelcut` (bundle, executable, module)" is now `PRODUCT_NAME`
  `Frame Job` in Release and Distribution, the bundle and executable following it in every
  configuration, and the module `FrameJob` in every configuration through `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME`.

"""Issue batch B70 (#220) — the spec indexes' Lines cells against `wc -l`,
and a row for every spec file. No app, no build, stdlib only.

`designs/spec/README.md` and `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md` each carry
a table whose rows read `` | [`<name>`](<link>) | <cell> | … ``. A FILE row's
cell is that file's line count (the number of newline bytes, what `wc -l`
prints). The FOLDER row (`11-decisions/`, linking its README) reads
`<N> in <M> files`: N is the summed line count of every `*.md` in the folder,
its README included, and M is how many there are. Every link must exist;
every `*.md` in `designs/spec/` but the README has exactly one row there,
every subdirectory has a folder row, and every `*.md` in `11-decisions/` but
its README has exactly one row in that README.

    python3 tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py             # the tree (make test)
    python3 tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py --selftest  # CONTROL + M1..M4

`--selftest` copies `designs/spec` to `tools/proof/work/spec_index/` (fresh)
and requires the copy to show 0 problems (CONTROL), then four mutants, each on
a fresh copy, to show exactly one problem naming its row: M1 the `07.6` row's
cell +1, M2 the `11-decisions/` folder cell's N +1, M3 the `deepening.md` cell
+1, M4 a new empty `zz-unindexed.md` beside the spec's files. Exit 0 when all
five hold, 1 otherwise.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
SPEC = os.path.join(ROOT, "designs", "spec")
WORK = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "proof", "work", "spec_index")
DECISIONS = "11-decisions"

ROW = re.compile(r"^\| \[`(?P<name>[^`]+)`\]\((?P<link>[^)]+)\) \| (?P<cell>[^|]+?) \|")
FOLDER_CELL = re.compile(r"^(\d+) in (\d+) files$")


def count_lines(path: str) -> int:
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        return handle.read().count(b"\n")


def index_rows(readme: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    rows = []
    for line in readme.splitlines():
        match = ROW.match(line)
        if match:
            rows.append((match["name"], match["link"], match["cell"].strip()))
    return rows


def markdown_files(folder: str) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(name for name in os.listdir(folder)
                  if name.endswith(".md") and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(folder, name)))


def check_index(spec_dir: str, folder: str, label: str, report: list) -> None:
    """One index (`<folder>/README.md`): its rows' cells and links, and a row
    for every `*.md` beside it and (for the top index) every subdirectory.
    Appends `(ok, text)` per check to `report`."""
    readme_path = os.path.join(folder, "README.md")
    with open(readme_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        rows = index_rows(handle.read())
    named = {}
    for name, link, cell in rows:
        named.setdefault(name, []).append(link)
        target = os.path.join(folder, link)
        if not os.path.exists(target):
            report.append((False, f"{label}: {name} links {link}, which does not exist"))
            continue
        report.append((True, f"{label}: {name} links {link}"))
        if name.endswith("/"):
            sub = os.path.join(folder, name.rstrip("/"))
            if link != f"{name}README.md":
                report.append((False, f"{label}: {name} links {link}, not {name}README.md"))
                continue
            files = markdown_files(sub)

69 CONTEXT.md
# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The probe builder (issue batch B88 phase 1a): the ONE swiftc line a proof,
a probe or the offscreen harness compiles app sources with, and its cache.

    python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py build --output PATH [--define D]… [--force] SOURCE…
    python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py typecheck [--define D]… [--sources DIR] PROBE.swift…
    python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py --selftest

`build()` compiles on every core (`-j <cores>`, or `-whole-module-optimization`)
into `work/swift-build/<key>/`. The key hashes this file, `swiftc --version`, the
SDK and its `SDKSettings.json`, the argv less its `-o`/`-j` values, the output's
file name (linked under it: the signature's identifier), the bytes of
every source, of the bridging header and each header it reaches by a quoted
`#include`, of the staticlib, the two encoder archives and their stamp
(`build/codecs/`, spec §11 CX-4: every app build links them, `codec_args()`) and each
link input, four toolchain variables and the tree's path (`#file` embeds it). An entry is reused only when its binary still
hashes to its manifest's digest, and is delivered to the caller's own path and
name (a bare binary's defaults domain and `proof_defaults.py --ran` are that name).
Every child runs under `bounded.run`, in its own process group; README: the selftest.
"""

import argparse
import contextlib
import fnmatch
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple, Sequence

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "graphics_spike"))
import bounded  # noqa: E402

CACHE = ROOT / "tools/proof/work/swift-build"
KEEP_ENTRIES = 32
BRIDGING = ROOT / "app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h"
LIBRARY = ROOT / "core/target/release/libframejob_core.a"
# The bundled encoders (road map "codec-export" C0): `make codecs` installs them, and
# every swiftc line that compiles app/Sources finds their headers and links them.
CODECS = ROOT / "build/codecs"
CODEC_ARCHIVES = (CODECS / "lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a", CODECS / "lib/libvpx.a")
CODEC_STAMP = CODECS / "stamp.json"
TARGET = "arm64-apple-macos26.0"
ENV_KEYS = ("DEVELOPER_DIR", "SDKROOT", "TOOLCHAINS", "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET")
STRIPPED = ("-o", "-j", "-output-file-map")  # flags whose VALUES the key ignores
INCLUDE = re.compile(r'^\s*#\s*include\s+"([^"]+)"', re.M)


class SwiftBuildFailed(RuntimeError):
    """`.diagnostics` (≤12 `error:` lines, else the tail), `.log` (None when nothing
    ran), `.expired` (the wall bound killed it), `.rc` (swiftc's status, or None)."""

    def __init__(self, message, diagnostics=(), log=None, expired=False, rc=None):
        super().__init__(message)

        self.log = log
        self.expired = expired
        self.rc = rc

    binary: Path
    key: str
    reused: bool
    seconds: float


def app_sources(folder=None):
    """Every `*.swift` in `folder` (default `app/Sources`) but `main.swift`, sorted."""
    folder = Path(folder) if folder is not None else ROOT / "app/Sources"
    return sorted(p for p in folder.iterdir() if p.suffix == ".swift" and p.name != "main.swift")


def _sha(path):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _label(path):
    path = Path(path).resolve()
    return str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) if path.is_relative_to(ROOT) else str(path)


_TOOLS = {}


def _tools():
    """swiftc's version and the SDK, read once per process."""
    if not _TOOLS:

            raise SwiftBuildFailed("swift_build: xcrun failed: "
                                   + (version["stderr"] + sdk["stderr"]).strip()[-300:])

        settings = Path(path) / "SDKSettings.json"
        _TOOLS.update(swiftc=(version["stdout"] + version["stderr"]).strip(), sdk=path,

    return _TOOLS

        if path in seen or not path.exists():
            continue

def _deliver(binary, output, expected=None):
    temp = Path(f"{output}.tmp-{os.getpid()}")
    temp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(binary, temp)
    if expected is not None and _sha(temp) != expected:  # the copy's bytes are the ones checked
        return os.unlink(temp)  # None: nothing delivered
    os.chmod(temp, 0o755)
    os.replace(temp, output)
    return True

"""The assistant's prompt texts, live context and evaluation — road map 12
A3 (spec §11 AI-7, AI-9, AI-15).

          what they say, and each

          live context block's; F8 holds each ask-first row's reason to a
          write (#158). `--probe` runs these alone:
          no app, no bun — the line `make test` runs.

`-RCSecretFolder`, `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` at the stand-in):
  S0  no `Frame Job: ` line
  S1  POST 1's system is `system`, a blank line, `search_guide`
  S2  the live context: in a saved project with the playhead at 2400000 and
      the text clip selected, turn 1's last user text is the exact
      <framejob_context> block, a newline and the person's text; after the
      playhead moves and the selection empties, turn 2 carries the new block
      and its `messages[0]` is turn 1's (append-only, AI-9)
  S3  a reply of 300000 input tokens makes the next POST, the summary,
      carry `compaction_instructions` verbatim
The evaluation (`assistant_prompt_eval.py`, imported), launch E on a scratch
socket, through the relay:
  E1–E6  six asks, each in a project of its own, judged by `get_project`
          placement only; an E row whose session met the month's budget FAILs
          `budget: …`, one that met the cap `cap: …`
  H   every POST the relay saw was within the bounds the arithmetic assumes
  K   the key's bytes in no file under work/assistant_prompt/ nor the app log

    python3 tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py --probe       # F, M (make test)
    python3 tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py               # F, M, S; E, H, K SKIP
    python3 tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py --rehearse [--wrong] [--cap D] [--month-spent D]
    python3 tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py --live --cap D   # needs the key
    python3 tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py --mutant bare-send   # S2 alone: FAILS

`--rehearse` points the relay at the stand-in with scripted right calls
(`--wrong`: the plausible mistakes, every E row must FAIL); `--cap` SETS the
cap, any positive figure: raising it is the runner's decision. `--live`
without `--cap` prints the headroom arithmetic and exits 2 before launching
anything.

The month's budget (spec §11 P-3, P-6): a keyed `--live` reserves every POST
in the proofs' ledger, `budget.LEDGER`, and nothing else ever opens it. A
rehearsal uses a scratch ledger, `work/assistant_prompt/rehearsal/spend.jsonl`,
deleted first; `--month-spent D` (rehearsal only) seeds it with D dollars
already spent this month, so `--month-spent 24.99` shows every E row refused
`budget:` with nothing sent to the stand-in. `--mutant bare-send` builds a tree copy (`tree_copy.make_copy`, into
`work/assistant_prompt/mutant/tree`) whose `send` writes the bare
text and runs S2 against it: it must FAIL (exit 1; 0 when it
survives); a copy that did not build exits 2, and so (rule R, issue batch
B13) does a run whose S2 was never scored or was scored by a caught
exception or a launch that could not run: `mutant <name>: the control could

"""The capture spike's Q2(c) inventory: which menu items reach a sheet, a
modal run loop, or neither — and the checks that hold `inventory.json` to
the tree (road map 11, V1).

`inventory.json` is READ BY HAND, site first: every line the grep below
finds is traced to the menu selectors that reach it, synchronously
(`reached_from`: the action method reaches the site before it returns) or
later (`reached_after`: from a sheet or panel completion, an async hop or an
AppKit delegate callback, with the `via` line and the `gate` that must hold).
Every other live selector is read to `none`, `window` or `framework`.
The grep counts the APP-MODAL `presentError(` (road map 11's V2b) — the
`presentError(_:)` / `NSApp.presentError(_:)` that runs a modal loop — and
not the sheet form `presentError(_:modalFor:…)`, which is not modal.

  I1  every leaf of `buildMainMenu()` (the probe's `menu` mode) has its
      selector in `selectors`, and every row there names a live selector;
  I2  the grep's sites and `sites` are one-to-one, each line holding its token
      and lying in its entry's `func`; a site is FOUND BY ITS TOKEN AND ITS
      ENCLOSING FUNCTION, not its line (#166, #168): `resolve` pairs the
      inventory's sites with the grep's per (file, token, func) — `func` the
      nearest `func NAME` or `init(` declaration at or above the line — in
      line order, whenever the two counts agree, so a line added above a
      site moves its pin instead of failing it; where they disagree each pin
      stands as written. A site removed and another added in one file and
      token no longer balance unless both are in one function, so a swap
      across functions is reported (K4);
  I3  every citation is checked for content (#168). A citation is a SITE ref,
      `app/Sources/<F>.swift:<N>` naming a key of `sites` (read at its
      resolved line), or an ANCHORED ref, ``app/Sources/<F>.swift `<anchor>` ``,
      whose anchor is a piece of the line meant and occurs exactly once in
      `<F>`. Each `code` item is exactly one citation; `note`, `via`, `gate`
      and `other_caller` hold citations in prose; any other `<F>.swift:<N>`
      is a problem, as is a line citation that is not a site, an anchor
      missing or not unique, and a `reached_after` whose `via` cites nothing.
      A `modal` selector cites a line holding a loop token, a `sheet` one a
      sheet token; every `reached_from` / `reached_after` selector names a
      row; a selector in the `reached_from` of a `runModal` or loop-token
      site is `modal` (`reached_after` never forces a verdict);
  I4  the checker over a copy missing one selector and one site reports
      exactly those two (the first selector no site references, and the
      first site no citation names by its line).

`python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.py --check` is a line of
`make test`: no app, no probe, no build, in a fresh `work/inventory_check/`.

  K1  I2 and I3 over the tree have no problem (I1 needs the probe, so it is
      `v2_menu.py`'s H1); its detail lists the pins found at another line;
  K2  CONTROL: a copy of `app/Sources` with three blank lines put at the top
      of every file that holds a site or is cited by an anchor has no I2 or
      I3 problem;
  K3  CONTROL: a fresh copy, the inventory's site keys first rewritten
      through `resolve`, then the line of the first rewritten site blanked:
      the checker reports exactly that site under I2;
  K4  CONTROL: a fresh copy, the keys rewritten, the first site's line
      blanked and `func b13Swap() { <that line> }` appended as the file's
      last line — a swap in one file and token: I2 reports exactly that site
      (its line does not hold its token) and the appended line (a grep site
      missing from the inventory);

11:- **The selection.** Click a clip to select it. ⇧-click adds a clip or takes it out. Drag from empty space to select by marquee. ⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select All**), ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**, every clip that starts at or after the playhead) and **Edit ▸ Select All on Track** also select. ⌥-clicking a track header selects every clip on that track. See [Timeline](timeline.md).
13:- **The in/out range.** I sets the in point, O sets the out point and ⌥X clears both (**Mark ▸ Set In / Set Out / Clear Range**). With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range instead.
32:The same two placements also work without dragging. Select a row in the Media tab, then choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**. They place the file on the current track at the playhead. Neither has a shortcut. Right-clicking a row gives you the same two items for that file. Both are greyed out when no media row is selected, and for a `.cube` LUT, which is applied as a look rather than placed (see [Colour grading](color-grading.md)).
64:To trim to the playhead, press **W** (**Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**) or **E** (**Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead**), or click the matching buttons in the timeline bar. They trim each selected clip that the playhead is inside. If the playhead isn't inside any selected clip, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. W undoes as "Trim Start" and E as "Trim End", one step for all the clips they trim.
89:**Clip ▸ Split** (⌘T, or the scissors button in the timeline bar) cuts at the playhead:
104:| **Edit ▸ Delete** (⌫) | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range and removes what lies between. Nothing moves, markers included. |
105:| **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** (⌘⌫, or the timeline bar's button) | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips, then closes each hole they leave. Everything later on every unlocked track moves left by the hole's length. | **Ripple Delete:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range, removes what lies between, and closes the hole. |
110:- **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…** and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** each make many ripple cuts as a single undo step. See [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md).
116:**Double-click an empty stretch of a lane** to close that gap. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. **Clip ▸ Close Gap** does the same for the gap under the playhead on the current track. A gap before the first clip of a track closes back to zero. Undo name: "Close Gap".
127:To open room by hand, press ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) and drag the selected clips later, or nudge them with ⇧. (period). Unlike Insert Time, this also moves selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are.
133:**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (⌘D, or the timeline bar's button) puts a copy of each selected clip on the same track, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing. The duplicate is refused if the copies would break the overlap rule. To place copies somewhere else, ⌥-drag instead (see [Moving clips](#moving-clips)).

142:| **Edit ▸ Cut** | ⌘X | Copies, then deletes the selection and leaves gaps, as ⌫ does. One undo step. |

144:| **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** | ⌥⌘V | Copies the copied clip's look onto every selected clip. |

11:- **The selection.** Click a clip to select it. ⇧-click adds a clip or takes it out. Drag from empty space to select by marquee. ⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select All**), ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**, every clip that starts at or after the playhead) and **Edit ▸ Select All on Track** also select. ⌥-clicking a track header selects every clip on that track. See [Timeline](timeline.md).
13:- **The in/out range.** I sets the in point, O sets the out point and ⌥X clears both (**Mark ▸ Set In / Set Out / Clear Range**). With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range instead.
32:The same two placements also work without dragging. Select a row in the Media tab, then choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**. They place the file on the current track at the playhead. Neither has a shortcut. Right-clicking a row gives you the same two items for that file. Both are greyed out when no media row is selected, and for a `.cube` LUT, which is applied as a look rather than placed (see [Colour grading](color-grading.md)).
64:To trim to the playhead, press **W** (**Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**) or **E** (**Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead**), or click the matching buttons in the timeline bar. They trim each selected clip that the playhead is inside. If the playhead isn't inside any selected clip, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. W undoes as "Trim Start" and E as "Trim End", one step for all the clips they trim.
89:**Clip ▸ Split** (⌘T, or the scissors button in the timeline bar) cuts at the playhead:
104:| **Edit ▸ Delete** (⌫) | **Delete:** removes the clips and leaves gaps. | **Lift:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range and removes what lies between. Nothing moves, markers included. |
105:| **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** (⌘⌫, or the timeline bar's button) | **Ripple Delete:** removes the clips, then closes each hole they leave. Everything later on every unlocked track moves left by the hole's length. | **Ripple Delete:** cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range, removes what lies between, and closes the hole. |
110:- **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…** and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** each make many ripple cuts as a single undo step. See [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md).
116:**Double-click an empty stretch of a lane** to close that gap. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. **Clip ▸ Close Gap** does the same for the gap under the playhead on the current track. A gap before the first clip of a track closes back to zero. Undo name: "Close Gap".
127:To open room by hand, press ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**) and drag the selected clips later, or nudge them with ⇧. (period). Unlike Insert Time, this also moves selected clips on locked tracks, and it leaves markers where they are.
133:**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (⌘D, or the timeline bar's button) puts a copy of each selected clip on the same track, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing. The duplicate is refused if the copies would break the overlap rule. To place copies somewhere else, ⌥-drag instead (see [Moving clips](#moving-clips)).
141:| **Edit ▸ Copy** | ⌘C | Puts the selected clips on the clipboard, with the media files they show. Pasted into a text editor, they arrive as a one-line summary such as "Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00". |
142:| **Edit ▸ Cut** | ⌘X | Copies, then deletes the selection and leaves gaps, as ⌫ does. One undo step. |
143:| **Edit ▸ Paste** | ⌘V | Pastes the clipboard's clips at the playhead, then selects them. |
144:| **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** | ⌥⌘V | Copies the copied clip's look onto every selected clip. |
145:| **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties** | — | Copies a copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips drawn by the same graphic. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |
166:**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (⌥⌘D) switches off each selected clip's sound and adds an audio-only copy of it on the track below, at the same time, with the same footage and speed. If the clip is on the back track, a new track is added behind it. Undo name: "Detach Audio".
180:**Clip ▸ Nest** (⌘G) groups the selected clips:

tool(
                "get_project",
                "The whole project as JSON: canvas (width, height, fps [num, den], background, "
                    + "fit_new_clips, timecode_frames), media, tracks, clips and markers, with "
                    + "next_id — the schema every op edits. Plus the state that is deliberately "
                    + "NOT in the model and lives only in the app: playhead, selection and the "
                    + "in/out range. Read this first: every other tool names things by the ids "
                    + "it reports, and clip, track, marker and media ids share ONE number space, "
                    + "so an id is unambiguous on its own. tracks[0] is the BACK of the layer "
                    + "stack (the bottom lane of the timeline); times are ticks at 600000 per "
                    + "second. missing_media lists media whose file has moved — relink_media "
                    + "points it at the new one. graphics: every module in the package's "
                    + "graphics/ with its revision, whether it compiles, and the clips drawn "
                    + "by it.",
                [:]),
            tool(
                "set_playhead",
                "Moves the playhead and seeks the preview. View state, not an edit: nothing is "
                    + "undoable and the project is untouched. split, freeze_frame and add_marker "
                    + "default to this time.",
                ["t": ["type": "integer", "description": "Time \(ticks)"]],
                required: ["t"]),
            tool(
                "set_range",
                "Sets the in/out range — Mark ▸ Set In (I) and Set Out (O). View state, not an "
                    + "edit: nothing is undoable and the project is untouched. Call it with NO "
                    + "bounds to clear the range (⌥X). export {range: \"in_out\"} writes only "
                    + "this span; get_project reports it as in_out_range.",
                [
                    "start": ["type": "integer", "description": "In point, \(ticks)"],
                    "end": ["type": "integer", "description": "Out point, \(ticks)"],
                ]),
            tool(
                "set_selection",
                "Selects clips — clicking one in the timeline or on the canvas, and Edit ▸ "
                    + "Select All (⌘A). View state like the playhead and the range: nothing is "
                    + "undoable and the project is untouched. It matters because the canvas "
                    + "handles, crop mode and every inspector pane act on the SELECTION, so "
                    + "this is how you put the app into the state a screenshot should show. "
                    + "Call it with no clips (or []) to select nothing; get_project reports the "
                    + "result as selection. Note that the ops themselves take their own clips "
                    + "argument — selecting is not a prerequisite for editing.",
                [
                    "clips": [
                        "type": "array", "items": ["type": "integer"],
                        "description": "Clip ids to select (get_project lists them). Omit or "
                            + "pass an empty array to select nothing.",
                    ]
                ]),
            tool(
                "set_scope",
                "Opens a nest so the app is LOOKING INSIDE it — double-clicking a nest clip "
                    + "in the timeline (Clip ▸ Open Nest, ⌘↓; Close Nest, ⌘↑). View state "
                    + "like the playhead and the selection: no op runs, nothing is undoable "
                    + "and the project is untouched. What it changes is what the app shows "
                    + "and therefore what get_project and render_frame answer — while a nest "
                    + "is open those report and draw that nest's own tracks, clips and frozen "
                    + "canvas rather than the timeline's, which is the only way to SEE what "
                    + "an edit inside one did. Name the nest, or the clip that shows it; call "
                    + "it with neither to come back out. While a nest is open every op you "
                    + "send lands INSIDE it unless the op's own scope argument says "
                    + "otherwise, exactly as an edit made by hand goes where the window is "
                    + "looking — so this is the setting to change first and the one to "
                    + "clear when you are done. Editing inside a nest does not require it: "
                    + "an op carrying scope works from wherever you are.",
                [
                    "nest": [
                        "type": "integer",
                        "description": "The nest to open, by id (get_project lists them under "
                            + "nests). It has to be shown by a clip on the TIMELINE: this is "
                            + "the view, and the app cannot show its way into a nest the "
                    "histogram": [
                        "type": "boolean",
                        "description": "Also measure the frame's histogram, View ▸ Scopes' "
                            + "Histogram: R′, G′, B′ and Y′ counts per 256 levels. The text says "
                            + "what share of pixels clips high and low by Y′, and <image "
                            + "path>.histogram.json holds the four planes' counts and both "
                            + "percentages. Default false.",
                    ],
                ]),
            tool(
                "export",
                "Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with "
                    + "{export_id, path, status} — ⌘E, the export sheet's six controls (format, "
                    + "size, frame rate, quality, loudness, range) in the sheet's own "
                    + "vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's "
                    + "rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The "
                    + "export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other "
                    + "export already there; status is queued or running. An av1, av1_webm "
                    + "or vp9_webm job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports "
                    + "would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later "
                    + "job may run first meanwhile (export_status's waiting says so). Follow "
                    + "it with "
                    + "export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until "
                    + "status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. "
                    + "The export_id lasts until Frame Job quits. Every refusal comes back "
                    + "from this call, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing "
                    + "folder, and a graphic clip whose module does not compile; a failure "
                    + "while writing comes back from export_status, failed with its reason "
                    + "(a graphic that fails during the export stops it with no file left, "
                    + "naming the graphic and the frame). The preset is the ENCODING only and "
                    + "the size a separate choice defaulting to the document's own, or on gif "
                    + "and apng to the format's cap; the core resolves both into concrete "
                    + "settings (container, codec, size, rate, range) and hands them to the "
                    + "same exporter the sheet uses, so an agent export and a menu export "
                    + "cannot disagree. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the "
                    + "container's extension is added when the path has none. In an HLG "
                    + "project (set_canvas output) hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, "
                    + "prores_422 and prores_4444 write HLG unless dynamic_range says pq or sdr, and every "
                    + "other video preset writes the project's SDR version. What the finished "
                    + "file holds is export_status's done answer.",
                [
                    "preset": exportPresetProperty,
                    "path": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Where to write, e.g. ~/Movies/cut.mp4. The folder must "
                            + "exist.",
                    ],
                    "size": exportSizeProperty,
                    "range": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["project", "in_out"],
                        "description": "What to write: the whole timeline (default), or just "
                            + "the in/out range set_range set — the sheet's Range popup.",
                    ],
                    "video_bitrate": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "Target video rate in BITS per second (8000000 is "
                            + "8 Mbps) — the sheet's Quality popup. Omit to let the preset's "
                            + "own encoder settings decide. Ignored by presets that carry no "
                            + "rate of their own: ProRes is fixed by its profile, and GIF and "
                            + "APNG have no bitrate at all. On av1 and av1_webm it is a soft "
                            + "cap: SVT-AV1 "
                            + "encodes at a constant quality matched to HEVC at this rate (HEVC's "
                            + "0.07 bits per pixel per frame when omitted), and the file usually "
                            + "stays under it; very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 "
                            + "times over. On vp9_webm it is a soft cap too: libvpx encodes at a "
                            + "constant quality matched to HEVC at this rate (HEVC 10-bit's in an "
                            + "HDR export), and the file usually stays under it; up to about "
                            + "1.15 times it was measured; on vp9_alpha_webm the cap is the "
                            + "picture's alone, its alpha at a constant quality.",
                    ],
                    "audio_bitrate": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "Target AAC or Opus rate in BITS per second (192000 "
                            + "is 192 kbps) — the sheet's Quality popup. Omit for 192 "
                            + "kbps. Ignored where the sound is neither: ProRes, WAV and AIFF "
                            + "all write LPCM, whose rate is its sample format.",
                    ],
                    "loudness_lufs": [
                        "type": "number", "minimum": -70, "maximum": 0,
                        "description": "Normalise the whole mix to this integrated loudness, "
                            + "in LUFS — the sheet's Loudness popup, whose rows are -14 "
                            + "(streaming), -16 (podcast) and -23 (EBU R 128 broadcast). The "
                            + "export measures itself first and then applies ONE gain to "
                            + "everything, so relative levels inside the timeline are "
                            + "untouched and no limiter is involved. Omit not to normalise: "
                            + "the export still measures and still reports. Ignored where "
                            + "there is no sound to measure (gif, apng).",
                    ],
                    "peak_dbtp": [
                        "type": "number", "minimum": -20, "maximum": 0,
                        "description": "The true-peak ceiling that gain is capped against, in "
                            + "dBTP. The sheet fixes it at -1 and this is the knob for "
                            + "anything else. Because normalisation is gain-only, a ceiling "
                            + "with no loudness_lufs beside it would have nothing to cap and "
                            + "is REFUSED rather than accepted and left inert. When the "
                            + "ceiling bites, the file lands quieter than the target asked "
                            + "for and the result's capped_by_peak says so.",
                    ],
                    "burn_in_timecode": burnInProperty,
                    // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-5, HD-14).

A wipe's edge is measured in each clip's own frame, so two clips of different sizes don't meet at one line.

A fade through a colour changes the layer's own pixels toward the colour. On a clip smaller than the canvas (a picture-in-picture), the fade shows a black (or white) box over what is behind it, not a see-through fade.

### Add a transition

There are three ways:

- **Overlap two clips.** Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the clip before it on the same track, and that clip has no transition stored, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve, eased (Ease In Out) and crossfading the sound. That holds whether you drag, trim an edge, paste, insert, close a gap or shift clips.
- **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ \<style\>.** Works on every selected clip at once:
  - A clip that already overlaps the clip before it gets the chosen style, keeping its curve and crossfade.
  - A clip at a **hard cut** (it starts exactly where the previous clip ends) gets a new half-second overlap, centred on the cut. The overlap is made from footage the two clips aren't showing: the source past the first clip's out point and before the second clip's in point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were. If there isn't half a second to spare, the transition comes out shorter.
  - A clip after a gap, or the first clip on its track, is skipped.

  A style is enabled only when at least one selected clip is at an overlap or a hard cut. The checkmark shows the first selected clip's style, or None when it has no transition. None is enabled for any selection.
- **The Transition section's Kind popup**, for a clip that already overlaps (below).

**When there is no footage to spare.** Two clips that each use their whole file have nothing beyond the cut to overlap with. Clip ▸ Transition ▸ then shows a sheet: "There's no extra footage at this cut for a transition." Choosing **Shift Clips Left** makes the overlap by sliding the second clip, and everything after it on unlocked tracks, left by half a second. The project gets that much shorter, and no clip's footage changes. Markers don't move. A clip on another track that ends up overlapping its neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve. The whole shift is one undo step. **Cancel** changes nothing.

*Agents:* `add_transition` (the hard-cut form: `kind`, `duration`, `align` `center`, `before` or `after`, and `ripple: true` for the Shift Clips Left form); `set_transition` (a kind onto a clip that already overlaps).

### The Transition section

The **Transition** section is on the Clip sub-tab when a single selected clip overlaps the clip before it. Its summary reads, for example, "cross dissolve · ease in out · 0.50 s", or "none".

| Row | What it does | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Kind | The style, or None | None and the thirteen styles |
| Curve | How the transition's progress is eased | Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out |

# Frame Job — design and implementation spec

**The normative spec, one file per section.** It was one 4,780-line file,
`designs/reelcut-design.md`, until 2026-09-26 (git history has it). Section numbers are
unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into
lettered files that keep its number (§4.3 is `04.3a`, `04.3b` and `04.3c`, §5.2 is `05.2a` and `05.2b`, §6 is `06a`, `06b` and `06c`, §7.5 is `07.5a` and `07.5b`, §7.9 is `07.9a`, `07.9b`, `07.9c` and `07.9d`);
a citation of the bare number names them together, and this index gets their rows in the same
change. Until #342 (2026-10-24) §4.3b was the Media, Document and Assistant tabs, now §4.3c; an older citation of §4.3b (in `archive/` or git history) means §4.3c.

The Lines column is `wc -l`; the `11-decisions/` cell is that folder's total, its README
included, and `make test` checks both (`tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`).

| File | Lines | Read it for |
|---|---|---|

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
## Rules

**Placement.** New feature = small model/value file + VC extension file +
gesture session struct (`ClipDragSession`, `TrimSession`, `CanvasSession` are
the template): one stored property on the view, logic in the feature's file.
Closures assigned in `loadView` are one-line forwards to named methods — no
business logic in closure bodies. New files are capped at 400 lines; a file
at the ~600-line cap gives something up first, as a pure move landed alone.

**Undo and dirty tracking.** All document mutation flows through
`ProjectDocument`'s entry points — `applyEdit`, `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)`
and the `beginLiveEdit`/`updateLiveEdit`/`endLiveEdit` trio for gestures.
`registerUndo` appears nowhere outside `ProjectDocument`. It overrides
`updateChangeCount` to drop AppKit's automatic counting; the entry points
count deterministically via `countEditChange()`. **Pitfall:** undo
registrations outside an AppKit event (agent edits, async callbacks) land in
the implicit event group AppKit never closes, silently merging edits into one
undo step; any off-event path goes through
`ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`. It opens its explicit group only for an
`.applied` answer (`commitEdit`, shared with `applyEdit`), so an identity, a
refusal or an error leaves the stack — redo included — untouched (#59).
`endLiveEdit(_:cancelled: true)` is the cancel path (Esc during a canvas
drag, `PreviewCanvasView.onLiveCancel`): it puts the `beginLiveEdit` snapshot
back and registers nothing, with no change count.
**Do not "flush" the manager to grouping level zero** to close that group: the
undo checkpoint `NSDocument` posts inside every save then raises, the
exception is swallowed inside the file coordinator, and ⌘S and `save_project`
hang for good.

**A refusal is the CORE's sentence, and nothing on this side writes one.**
An op answers `.applied`, `.identity` or `.refused` (`ReelEdit.swift`); a
person hears a beep for both non-applied arms and, for a refusal, reads the
core's sentence verbatim after "Refused: " at the inspector's foot (spec
§11 CI-10), and an agent hears
`<Action> made no change: the project is already in that state.` or
`<Action> was refused at <op>: <the rule's own sentence>`, written once in
`AgentServer.performGroupedEdit`. **No handler applies an op to see what
would happen and then writes its own reason**, and none re-derives a rule's
arithmetic to predict one. Spec §11's **D2-1** is the line: a check that
predicts a RULE goes, a check that names the CALL stays — an argument a
handler cannot read or was not given (`AgentServer+Arguments.swift`), or a
composite's own reading, like `normalize_clip` with nothing it could
MEASURE. Prose that TEACHES a rule before the call belongs in a tool
description; prose that explains a refusal after it is the core's to write.

**Two callers swallow a refusal on purpose.** `ReelProject.scoped(_:)` drops
the core's message because every caller is a VIEW asking about view state
`clampViewState` has already cleared, so a nil is a race with an undo and
not a failure to report. `ProjectDocument.updateLiveEdit` swallows every
answer but `.applied` because a refused tick is NORMAL mid-drag — the edge
is past a neighbour for a moment — and recovers on the next one with the
last good frame still on screen, where a drag that spoke would interrupt the
gesture to say what the person is already fixing with the mouse;
`endLiveEdit` then registers no step at all. Neither is a gap to be closed
(kpgalligan/framejob#8's eighth decision).

**Lenient decoding is for what the CORE wrote; nothing a caller wrote is
decoded through it.** `ProjectSnapshot`/`MotionProps`' `lenient` and
`nullable` exist so a project, plan, recipe or export setting a NEWER build
wrote still opens — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, an unreadable
value a default or a clear. Run over an agent's own object that same
leniency is a silent correction, so a caller-authored object (a patch, a

## Volume

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volume | The clip's level as a percentage. Quick picks: 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 400. | 0–400 % | 100 % |
| Gain | Read-only: the volume in dB (for example "+6.0 dB"), or "silent" at 0 %. | — | +0.0 dB |
| Mute | Silences the clip without changing its volume. | on / off | off |
| Normalize | Sets the volume from the clip's own loudest moment (see below). | — | — |

The section's summary reads "muted", "silent" or the gain in dB. Reset puts the volume back to 100 % and turns Mute off.

You can animate volume, Mute and the fades with actions. While an action is selected, the Volume row, the Mute checkbox and the Fade in and Fade out rows write that action's end state, so a level moves across the action's span. Pan, Mix to mono, Keep pitch, the compressor, noise reduction and ducking can't be animated. They always change the clip's own settings, even with an action selected.

### Normalize

## Splitting

**Clip ▸ Split** (⌘T, or the scissors button in the timeline bar) cuts at the playhead:

- With clips selected, it cuts each selected clip the playhead is strictly inside.
- With nothing selected, it cuts every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track.

The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped. Animation actions stay with the piece they fall in, and an action that spans the cut becomes two. Caption word timings stay on their words.

*Agents:* `split` takes `at` (the playhead when left out) and optional `clips`. Without `clips` it cuts every unlocked clip at that time.

## Deleting
## Text clips

Press **T**, or use the timeline bar's **Add Text** button, to add a text clip
at the playhead. It goes on the front-most track if there is room, or on a new
track in front of everything if there isn't. The new clip:

- reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, white, centred
- lasts 5 seconds
- is selected, so the **Text** sub-tab opens on it

A text clip has no source file, so you can trim it to any length.
Double-click it on the canvas to type (see
[Inline text editing](#inline-text-editing)).

*Agents:* `add_text_clip` (track, at, optional duration and text, either a
plain string or a text patch); `set_text` to restyle.

### The Text tab

| Section | Rows |
# Exporting

Frame Job writes the timeline out as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and saves single frames as stills. One export sheet covers every format. You choose the format, then the size, frame rate, quality, loudness and range, and the sheet shows what the file will be before anything is written. Exports can run at once behind a progress sheet, or wait in the Export Queue while you keep editing. Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured.

## Opening the export sheet

Choose **File ▸ Export…** (⌘E), or click **Export…** at the right end of the toolbar. Playback pauses and the sheet opens over the editor window.

The command is greyed out while the timeline is empty. An export always writes the whole top-level timeline, even when you are working inside a nest.

The sheet reopens on the **last choices you exported with**. Clicking **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them; Cancel does not. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not to the project, so every document's sheet opens on it. A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document that has no range.

## The controls

From top to bottom:

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Preset** | Applies a saved set of choices (see [Presets](#presets)). The gear beside it saves and deletes presets. | Custom |
| **Format** | The encoding: container and codec together. | H.264 (MP4) |
| **Dynamic Range** | Shown only in an HDR (HLG) project. See [HDR projects](#hdr-projects). | HDR (HLG) |
| **Speed** | How long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. See [Speed](#speed). | Balanced |
| **Size** | The frame size, or **Custom…** with width and height fields on the row below. | The format's first row |
| **Frame rate** | **Project rate**, or a fixed rate. | Project rate |
| **Quality** | **Format default**, or a bit-rate tier. | Format default |
| **Loudness** | **Off**, a loudness target, or **Custom…** with a LUFS field. | Off |
| **Range** | **Whole project**, or **In/out range** when one is set. | Whole project |
| **Burn in timecode** | Draws the project timecode into the picture. | Off |

Under the controls, a readout line describes the file and a footnote names the codec, the container and the rates the file will use. Every number they show is the size, rate and duration the file will actually have.

- **Readout:** `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` (size, frame rate, duration). For the audio-only formats it reads `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`. For GIF and APNG it adds the frame count: `· 360 frames, no audio`. For **AV1 (MP4)**, **AV1 (WebM)**, **VP9 (WebM)** and **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** a second line estimates how long the export will take: `Estimated time: about 25 s` (in 5-second steps under a minute, then minutes, then hours and minutes). It follows the format, Speed, size and range, and it is only an estimate: the figures behind it are the median of three measured exports per format at 1080p and 4K, of real 4K camera footage on an idle Apple M2 Max, so a slower or busy Mac, or a heavy timeline, takes longer. The other formats show no estimate.
- **Footnote:** the codec, the container (left out when it is the same word, as in `GIF`), the AV1 speed (`AV1 · MP4 · Balanced`, `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`; VP9 has none: `VP9 · WEBM`, `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`), the video rate, the audio rate (`192 kbps audio`), the loudness target (`−14 LUFS`) and `alpha` when the format keeps transparency. When you pick a Quality tier and the format sets its own rate, it reads `format's own rate` instead of a number.

A control the chosen format cannot use is greyed out rather than hidden. Its value is not sent.

### Format

### Range

**Whole project** writes the whole timeline. **In/out range** writes only the range set on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)), snapped to the export's frame grid. The popup is greyed out when there is no range.

Inside a nest, the popup is greyed out even when the nest has a range, and its tooltip says why: an export writes the whole timeline, so it cannot use a range that belongs to the nest. Leave the nest (⌘↑) and set the range on the timeline.

### Burn in timecode

is never read. A step is skipped when its hash equals its last pass. The

input.content: # Spec: Tutorials TU0 (decisions, words) + TU1 (five model tutorials as text, extractor, target table, checker) ## Goal Record TU-1..TU-6 in spec §11 (TU-2 holding the normative step vocabulary below), write the five model tutorials of `designs/tutorials.md` §6 into their guide pages, bundle them as `Tutorials.json`, and add the app's spotlight-target table. `make test` gains `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py`, which fails by page and step on anything the vocabulary, the catalog, the table, the menu bar or the clip schema does not have. ## Files - `designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` — NEW: header in `dev-tools.md`'s style; TU-1..TU-6 as road map §9 words them; TU-2 holds the vocabulary of **Interfaces §A** verbatim in substance; TU-3 includes the menu form and the list form of Show Me - `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md` — file row (Lines = `wc -l`) after `codec-export.md`; six rows TU-1..TU-6 appended to "Every decision" - `designs/spec/README.md` — the `11-decisions/` cell (`N in 34 files`) - `CONTEXT.md` — **Tutorial** and **Practice project** at the end of "Language", in its `**Term**:` / prose / `_Avoid_:` shape, wording from road map §3 - `designs/tutorials.md` — §4.2 gets one line: normative text is spec §11 TU-2 (TU1 added `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, list and menu Show Me, `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range.changed`, `follows_clip`); §9 TU1 names TU-2 as the vocabulary's home; "Record" gets the TU0+TU1 entry (landed, measured — numbers only as printed —, review, owed) - `docs/guide/audio.md` — `### Tutorial: change a clip's volume` at the end of `## Volume` (before `### Normalize`) - `docs/guide/editing.md` — `### Tutorial: split a clip` at the end of `## Splitting` - `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md` — `### Tutorial: add a title` at the end of `## Text clips` (before `### The Text tab`) - `docs/guide/motion-and-transitions.md` — `### Tutorial: cross-dissolve two clips` after `### Add a transition` - `docs/guide/export.md` — `### Tutorial: export a range` at the end of `### Range` - `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` — NEW: parser (shared with the checker) + `--guide DIR --out FILE` writer; stdlib only; ≤400 lines - `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift` — NEW: the target table (**Interfaces §C**); nothing calls it but the probe yet; ≤400 lines - `tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift` — NEW: compiled as `main.swift` over `swift_build.app_sources()` with `-D FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` through `swift_build.build()`; prints one `ANSWER` line (**Interfaces §D**) - `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` — NEW: the checker (**Interfaces §E**) - `tools/proof/tutorial_fixtures/` — NEW: `guide/model.md` (one valid tutorial using every vocabulary key), `facts.json` (a probe answer in miniature), `inventory.json` (a `selectors` object), `sources/Sections.swift` (section literals in `id: "x", title:` form) - `project.yml` — postBuildScripts "Write Tutorials" after "Copy Graphic Templates": `basedOnDependencyAnalysis: false`, `export PATH="/usr/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"`, `python3 "$PROJECT_DIR/tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py" --guide "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/guide" --out "$TARGET_BUILD_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH/Tutorials.json"`, with a comment in the file's style - `Makefile` — `python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` after `spec_index_proof.py` in `test`; `--ran tutorial_probe` added to the `proof_defaults.py` line; one sentence in the comment block above `test:` - `tools/proof/gate.py` — `STEP_INPUTS["app"]`: roots `+ "docs/guide", "tools/tutorials"`, kept md `+ "docs/guide/"`; selftest `classes` + `("M3", "docs/guide/audio.md", {"names","test","app"})`, `("M8", "tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py", {"names","test","app"})` - `tools/proof/proof_app.py` — `LISTED += "docs/guide/*.md", "tools/tutorials/*.py"`; `KEPT_MD = ("docs/graphics-api.md", "docs/guide/")` and line 136 reads `relative.startswith(KEPT_MD)` - `tools/proof/README.md` — new section `## Tutorials checked (tutorial_check.py)` at the end (CLI, rows, selftest cases, what the probe prints, ~build time as printed); the gate section's `app` input list and `*.md` sentence updated - `docs/developing.md` — a `tools/tutorials/` row in the layout block after `tools/licenses/` ## Interfaces **§A Vocabulary (TU-2, closed; the checker refuses anything else).** - Structure: a heading `### Tutorial: `; its next non-blank line starts `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's continuation lines are indented ≥3 spaces; an item may end with `<!-- step {json} -->` (JSON may span lines); nothing follows `-->` in the item; no `<!-- tutorial`/`<!-- step` anywhere else. The sentence = the item's text minus the comment, lines joined by one space; non-empty; Markdown kept. - Tutorial keys: `id` (required, `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`, unique across the guide), `needs` (optional) `{"clip": <filter>}`. - Clip filter: optional `has_sound` bool, `has_pixels` bool, `kind` ∈ `media still image text shape graphic nest adjustment`, `follows_clip` bool (starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its track). `{}` = any clip. - Step keys (all optional): `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional` (`true`: Skip offered, not required). - `reveal`: `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <ClipSubTab raw>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` clip; `section` must be in the table and its home equal (`tab`, `sub_tab`). - `spotlight`: one string — a fixed name, `section:<id>` (id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. - `wait` (≥1 condition, all must hold): `selection` `{min? int≥0 (default 1), max? int≥min, …filter keys}` (every selected clip matches); `changed` path or [paths] (a dotted clip-JSON path; met when any clip selected at step start differs there from step start); `clips` `{added: int≥1, kind?}`; `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range` exactly one of `{set: true}` / `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. No `wait` = Next. - `show_me`: `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}` | `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}` | a non-empty list of those, run in order. Tool: in the catalog, not in `dev_tools`; every args key in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the property has `enum` must be a member; for `set_video|set_audio|set_text|set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch` as `<group>.<path>` must resolve in the fixture clips. Menu: an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf selector is a key of `inventory.json`'s `selectors`. - Variables (inside `show_me` args only, any depth): `"$selection"` → ids at step start; `"$created"` → ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"` → tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}` → id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: front track first); `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}` → earliest id; `{"$time": {"of": <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}` → tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}` → front track id. `<ref>` = `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick` or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused. - Sentence menu paths: `▸` only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`, which must be a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf selector is in `inventory.json`. **§B `Tutorials.json`** (`json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`, pages sorted by file name, only pages with tutorials): `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page": "audio.md", "title": "<the page's H1>", "tutorials": [{"id", "title", "anchor" (GitHub slug of the heading), "needs" (default {}), "steps": [{"text", …the step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}` **§C Swift** (`TutorialTargets.swift`): ```swift struct TutorialSectionHome: Equatable { let tab: InspectorTab; let subTab: ClipSubTab? } enum TutorialTargets { static let sectionPrefix = "section:" static let clipPrefix = "clip:" static let clipRefs: [String] // ["$selection", "$created"] static let fixed: [String: String] // name → the control, one line each static let sections: [String: TutorialSectionHome] // every InspectorSection id literal in app/Sources static func manifest() -> [String: Any] // {"fixed":[sorted],"sections":{id:{"tab","sub_tab"|null}},"clip_refs","tabs","sub_tabs"} } ``` Fixed names: `timeline.clips`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`, `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<InspectorTab title lowercased>` and `inspector.sub_tab.<ClipSubTab raw>` (built from `allCases`), `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,cancel}`. Homes come from `ClipPane.makeSections()` (sound/text/shape/graphic/picture/color/clip), `DocumentPane` (`document`, nil), `MediaPane` (`media`, nil); `video.shadow` → picture. **§D Probe answer**: `ANSWER {"tools": {name: {"properties": {…}}}, "dev_tools": [AgentServer.devToolNames sorted], "targets": TutorialTargets.manifest(), "menu": [{"path": [titles], "selector": str|null, "submenu": bool}], "clips": [<the fixture project's clips array as the core writes it>]}`. Setup as `assistant_lane_probe.swift`'s (prohibited policy, `AppDelegate().applicationWillFinishLaunching`, `AgentLane.prepareAtLaunch()`, then `AgentServer.shared.preparedCatalog`); the menu walked from `NSApp.mainMenu` as `probe_sheets.swift`'s `runMenu` does; fixture = `ReelProject.new` + ops: one media clip with picture and sound (stand-in `add_media` descriptor, no file), one text clip, one shape clip, no overlap. **§E Python**: ```python # tutorial_extract.py class Problem(NamedTuple): page: str; line: int; tutorial: str | None; step: int | None; message: str def parse_page(name: str, text: str) -> tuple[dict | None, list[Problem]] def parse_guide(folder: Path) -> tuple[dict, list[Problem]] # §B document def main(argv=None) -> int # exit 1, printing "<page>:<line>: <message>", on any Problem # tutorial_check.py def build_facts() -> dict # swift_build.build + run; raises ProbeFailed (a scored FAIL, exit 1) def check(document: dict, facts: dict, inventory: dict, sources: Path) -> list[Problem] def selftest() -> int def main(argv=None) -> int # [--facts FILE] [--save-facts FILE] [--selftest] ``` Output: `FAIL <page> tutorial <id> step <n>: <message>` per problem, then `tutorial_check: <T> tutorials, <S> steps, <P> problems`; exit 0 iff P = 0. `check` also reports every table section id absent from the `id: "<x>", title:` literals in `sources`, and every such literal absent from the table. ## Approach 1. TU0: write `tutorials.md` (§11), the two README edits, `CONTEXT.md`. Run `spec_index_proof.py`. 2. `TutorialTargets.swift`; `make typecheck` (baseline 0 errors, 4 warnings). 3. `tutorial_extract.py`; then the five tutorials, each sentence true for a reader with no runner: - **audio.volume** needs `{clip:{has_sound:true}}`: (1) select a clip with sound — `timeline.clips`, wait `selection {has_sound:true}`, show_me `set_selection {clips:[{$pick:{has_sound:true}}]}`; (2) open the Clip tab's **Sound** sub-tab, find Volume, drag or pick a level — reveal clip/sound/`audio.volume`, `section:audio.volume`, `changed "audio.volume"`, `set_audio {clips:"$selection", patch:{volume:1.5}}`; (3) optional, press Space — `toolbar.play`, `playing`. - **editing.split** needs `{clip:{}}`: select a clip (`$pick {}`); put the playhead inside it — `ruler`, `playhead {inside:"$selection"}`, `set_playhead {t:{$time:{of:"$selection",at:"middle"}}}`; I've written the spec for TU0+TU1 at /Users/kevingalligan/.claude/litecode/framejob/tutorials-tu0-tu1/01-spec.md. It is 118 lines, follows spec-template.md, and needed no STOP. Nothing was run; this stage only read the repo.

**What it covers:**
- **TU0:** the spec §11 file `designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` with TU-1..TU-6, its rows in `11-decisions/README.md`, the folder total in `designs/spec/README.md`, and the two terms in `CONTEXT.md`.
- **The step vocabulary:** I put the normative text in spec §11 TU-2. The road map's §4.2 gets a one-line pointer to it.
- **The five tutorials:** each step is spelled out (wait, reveal, spotlight, Show Me), with the place in each of the five guide pages where it goes.

**New files:**
- `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py`, run by a new "Write Tutorials" build step in `project.yml` to produce `Tutorials.json`.
- `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`, the target-name table.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`, built through `swift_build.py`.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` with `--selftest`, plus its fixtures.

**Edited:** `Makefile`, `gate.py` and `proof_app.py`. The last two now count the guide pages and the extractor as inputs of the app.

**Where I departed from the request or the road map:**
1. **Menu paths.** `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json` lists menu selectors, not menu paths. So the checker reads paths from the menu bar the probe builds (`buildMainMenu()`), and checks each path's selector against `inventory.json`.
2. **Catalog, section ids and the `changed` schema can't be read statically.** The catalog only exists in the built app bundle, and `make test` builds no app. So `tutorial_check` builds a probe from `app/Sources`, which prints:
   - the prepared catalog, the dev-tool names, the target table and the menu bar;
   - the clip JSON the core writes for three fixture clips (media with picture and sound, text, shape). `changed` paths and Show Me patch keys are checked against those clips.
   - Section ids are checked both ways: against the table, and against the `id: "x", title:` literals in `app/Sources`.
   - Cost: the probe takes about 100 s to rebuild after a Swift change, by analogy with the existing probes; nothing has measured it yet.
3. **Vocabulary added beyond road map §4.2:**
   - Variables `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time` and `$track` (Show Me for split, the playhead step, add title and export needs them).
   - Show Me as a list of calls, so adding the title can also select the new clip.
   - A menu form of Show Me, `{"menu": "A ▸ B"}`, because opening the export sheet has no product tool. TU-3 is worded to allow it.
   - `export_started` replaces `queued`, because the sheet's Export… isn't a queue job.
   - `range.changed`, and the clip filter `follows_clip`.
4. **Transition length.** A transition stores no duration. Its length is the overlap, so the cross-dissolve's Duration step waits on `changed: "start"`.

**Selftest:** 14 cases, one per kind of refusal the request names. The spec records that as the reason for going past the usual 10.

**Left for later phases:** how Show Me behaves while the export sheet is open is TU2's, and is listed under Out of scope.

**CLAUDE.md edits owed** (for you to apply):
- Root map: add the `tools/tutorials/` row.
- Root `make test` line: add `tutorial_check.py` and `--ran tutorial_probe`.
- Root: note the "Write Tutorials" build step.
- `app/CLAUDE.md`: a map entry for `TutorialTargets.swift`.

No owner choices came up.
